identity.one_liner: Considered, small-batch fashion in natural fibres for people who buy less but buy better.
identity.target_customer: 28-45 year old urban professionals who value craftsmanship and provenance over trend cycles; low purchase frequency, high average order value, researches before buying.
value_props: Made-to-last construction, not seasonal trend cycles

tone.voice_notes: Reads like a design journal, not an ad. Leads with craft and material story before price or promotion.

competitors.name: Nicobar
competitors.positioning_note: Closest direct competitor, similar handloom/considered-design ethos.

customers.summary: Skews premium and loyal-core: low discount-code usage, high AOV, low cart-abandonment, values exclusivity over price.

brand.semantic.competitors.name: Nicobar
brand.semantic.competitors.positioning_note: Closest direct competitor, similar handloom/considered-design ethos.

market_memory.patterns.pattern_statement: Adding explicit size/fit reassurance (try-on video, size-chart callout, fit guide) to the product page tends to reduce cart abandonment.
Creator/customer-style short-form video content tends to outperform polished static product imagery on engagement.

brief.buyer_power: Low, driven by the loyal-core segment's high Average Order Value, low discount usage, and strong preference for provenance and craftsmanship over price.
brief.supplier_power: Moderate, tied to the reliance on small-batch natural fiber production, which implies specific sourcing constraints that can be leveraged against mass producers.
brief.competitive_rivalry: Moderate, as direct competitors exist (Nicobar, Bombay Shirt Company, Okhai) operating in a similar premium/considered-design space, but differentiation based on unique maker stories and material focus provides some separation.
brief.threat_of_substitutes: Moderate, substitutes exist in general fashion or lower-cost artisanal goods, but the specific value proposition of traceable, small-batch luxury acts as a strong barrier against easy substitution for this segment.
brief.threat_of_new_entrants: Low to Moderate, due to the high barrier to entry associated with authentic craftsmanship, specialized sourcing, and building the necessary traceable maker story required to compete effectively in the premium slow fashion niche.
brief.positioning_summary: Loom & Aster benefits from strong customer loyalty and a premium positioning based on unique value props (traceability, small-batch natural fibers). Margin defense relies on maintaining this differentiation against entrants who might attempt to mimic the aesthetic without replicating the authentic craft story.

constraints.product: Focus on the unique material composition and the small-batch nature of the creation.
constraints.price: Maintain premium pricing posture; absolutely no discount, sale, or promotional language allowed.
constraints.place: Curated digital presentation reflecting an editorial design journal aesthetic.
constraints.promotion: Strictly editorial tone. All messaging must prioritize the maker/sourcing story over product features or price. No discount language whatsoever.
constraints.people: Highlight the craftspeople, makers, and sourcing origins as central figures in the narrative.
constraints.physical_evidence: Imagery must evoke a design journal feel; focus on texture, material quality, and the origin of the fibers.
constraints.process: Emphasize traceability, the slow process of creation, and the artisanal methods used in sourcing and making.
hard_rules: This line never goes on sale
Make the maker/sourcing story front and center
